R1.risk: A recipient re-identifies applicants in the research extract by linking it to a public list
R1.evidence: Release A linked 99.2% of the register's applicants; after treatment no register record matched a single record; classes can still share one sensitive value
R1.affected: 60,000 applicants; income, disability and support status

R2.risk: Ahliya declines eligible applicants, more often non-Saudi women and the self-employed
R2.evidence: FNR 30% for eligible non-Saudi women against 22% for others; 65% for the self-employed; group thresholds narrow the gap to 10 points
R2.affected: 1,444 of 6,341 eligible applicants in the reviewed sample declined by the screen; housing support delayed or lost

R3.risk: The district dashboard is misread, or its budget is overspent by monthly refreshes
R3.evidence: Relative error 3.1% in the ten smallest districts at epsilon 0.5; a monthly refresh at 0.5 spends 6 a year
R3.affected: public trust in the statistics; applicants in small districts

R4.risk: The hackathon file is regenerated with a setting that copies applicants
R4.evidence: Leaves of one row copied 92.8% of training rows (membership AUC 0.819); leaves of 200 passed (0.511)
R4.affected: the 8,000 applicants in the generator's training rows
